messages:
maria_support: Customer reported that their daily 'Consumption' tile in the Console shows a big spike that starts at 23:00 and continues into the next calendar day for their org. They say the exported CSV also splits the same day's tokens into two rows. 
eli_engineer: Can you paste the org timezone and an example export CSV row?
carol_ops: Org tz is 'America/Chicago' (CST/CDT), customer account id 0452-xx. Example CSV line they sent: 
`2026-10-31T23:30:12Z,org_0452,model-x,587` 
They expect that 23:30 local -> 18:30 UTC and should be counted on 2026-10-31 local, but dashboard shows it on 2026-11-01 bucket.
sanjay_product: Hmm, so chart tiles and the export disagree on the bucket boundary? Which one is using org tz?
maria_support: From what we can tell: the chart in Console appears to roll day boundaries at UTC midnight for some tiles; export file has rows stamped in UTC but named with local date by the UI which mismatches. Customer noticed this after DST end last week. :confused:
eli_engineer: Adding a quick repro I ran on staging: I sent three incremental generate calls with timestamps around the DST rollback (2026-11-01 01:30 local). Ingest shows events with server_ts in UTC, and aggregation job does: `date_trunc('day', received_at)` without timezone awareness. That will bucket in UTC.
eli_engineer: Paste of aggregation snippet from code: 
```
-- aggregation job
SELECT date_trunc('day', received_at) as bucket_utc, org_id, sum(tokens) FROM ingested_events GROUP BY 1,2;
```
carol_ops: That explains it. If received_at is stored as timestamptz but we don't convert to org timezone before truncation, buckets will be UTC. We need `received_at AT TIME ZONE org_tz` or use timezone-aware trunc.
maria_support: Customer is concerned about billing implications — they saw one day undercounted and the next day overcounted, which affects their daily dashboards used for internal alerts. They're asking for timeline and whether historical exports will change.
sanjay_product: Short-term: we should add a support note clarifying that Historical CSVs are UTC-stamped and the Console labels dates in org tz, causing apparent shifts at boundaries. Long-term: fix aggregation to bucket by org timezone and backfill.
eli_engineer: Proposed fix: in aggregator, compute `date_trunc('day', (received_at AT TIME ZONE 'UTC') AT TIME ZONE org_tz)`. Also ensure DST aware tz library when deriving org_tz. I'll open an RFC/PR.
maria_support: For now asked to provide customer with repro steps so they can verify: 
1) Pick an org with non-UTC tz (e.g., America/Chicago).
2) Generate a token event at 2026-11-01T05:30:00Z (which is 00:30 CDT).
3) Download daily export for 2026-11-01 and check which side the token landed on.

maria_support: Customer wants a quick mitigation: can we add a Console tooltip explaining that exports are UTC and charts use org timezone?
sanjay_product: Agree, add tooltip and an incident note. Prioritize aggregator fix P1 for next sprint + backfill job to re-bucket last 30 days.
eli_engineer: I'll create the PR and the one-off backfill job. tagging @ingest-bot to kick a test run on staging: `ingest-bot: run-backfill --org=0452 --days=40 --dry-run`
ingest-bot: Backfill dry-run queued for org_0452. Estimated rows to move: 1,242. ETA ~ 12m.
maria_support: Thanks — I'll update the customer with repro steps, the tooltip plan, and an ETA for the backfill. :thumbsup:
